## November 3 evening report and its first-part copy

**Sources on this page:** p112 A1, p112 A2, p112 A3. [Concise case study](../military/nov3_evening_report.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p111 A1](111.md#source-p111-a1).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov3-evening-report-november-3-evening-report-and-its-first-part-copy"></a>



**Status:** four physical records: the first-part witness on p111 and all
three source-marked parts on p112. The two first parts support seventeen
previously erased coordinates, while two observed coordinate conflicts
remain explicit. The damaged second and third parts have separately priced
editorial readings and three unresolved positions.

The p112 header gives an origin of 2030 (3), a receipt of 2.33 a.m. on
November 4 and three parts. The p111 witness is received at 3.44 a.m. on
November 4; its sender is missing and its recipient is NKJ. Both pages are
headed November 3. The source images are [p111](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/sources/p111_full.png)
and [p112](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/sources/p112_full.png).

The readable passages retain every edited label other than X separators;
case, punctuation and German umlaut/ss display forms are normalized.
A separate character-level mapping checks this correspondence. The literal
`A`, doubled separator, strange date/reference labels and repeated `TLICH`
remain. No abbreviation is expanded into a person's identity.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov3-evening-report-p111-a1"></a>

### p111 A1

The source has 202 slots, including three complete five-dash groups. All fifteen source-mask fills are supplied by the p112 witness. The single observed repair selects UJVIDEK at its first occurrence; the second occurrence is unchanged in both copies.

<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame:**

```text
OKMXOK?XABENDMEL?UNGXANSA?EXDONAUXR?HEALPXKO?P?ERREICH?R?UMSUED?I?HUJVINE?X?JVIDEK?2?9219IDUXG?KX5353
```

**Edited output — priced editorial candidate under the same stated frame:**

```text
OKMXOKMXABENDMELDUNGXANSAVEXDONAUXRUHEALPXKORPSERREICHTRAUMSUEDLICHUJVIDEKXUJVIDEKX219219IDUXGXKX5353
```

</details>

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> OKM. OKM. Abendmeldung. An Save, Donau Ruhe. Alp. Korps erreicht Raum südlich Ujvidek. Ujvidek. 219219IDU. G. K. 5353.

The candidate uses **1 observed-coordinate substitution**, **15 source-mask fills** and **0 unprinted-coordinate fills**. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

### p112 A1

This source also has 202 slots. Visible C in XGCXV and R in AARVA remain literal invalid-coordinate glyphs; the other copy supplies G and F. The ordinary DONOU → DONAU repair is separate.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame:**

```text

```

**Edited output — priced editorial candidate under the same stated frame:**

```text

```

</details>

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> OKM. OKM. Abendmeldung. An Save, Donau Ruhe. Alp. Korps erreicht Raum südlich Ujvidek. Ujvidek. 219219IDU. G. K. 5353.

The candidate uses **1 observed-coordinate substitution**, **2 source-mask fills** and **0 unprinted-coordinate fills**. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

There are **183 identical observed coordinates**, seventeen one-sided
erasures and two conflicting observed coordinates. All four common streams
have the same minimum combined cost of two observed substitutions. The
chosen readable stream selects DONAU from p111 and UJVIDEK from p112;
copying alone does not make either conflicting value unanimous.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov3-evening-report-p112-a2"></a>

### p112 A2

The native 218-slot source includes four complete five-dash groups. The older OCR lost one entire group and produced a misleading 213-slot frame. This is the most editorially uncertain part: the raw JAEVZE?G and ?ELLRA? are not independently proved to be FAHRZEUG and BELGRAD. Their repairs are priced, and two reference positions remain unknown.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame:**

```text
??ETENAX41??X11XMAD??HNACHNOR??STENANXX?UFTAUFKLA?RUNGXSTA?KENJAEVZE?GVERK?HR?SEMEN?RIA?ELLRA?XG?NXSTA?SXO?FZ
```

**Edited output — priced editorial candidate under the same stated frame:**

```text
TRETENAX41??X11XMARSCHNACHNORDOSTENANXXLUFTAUFKLAERUNGXSTARKENFAHRZEUGVERKEHRXSEMENDRIABELGRADXGENXSTABSXOFFZ
```

</details>

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> Treten A 41?? / 11. Marsch nach Nordosten an. Luftaufklärung starken Fahrzeugverkehr Semendria Belgrad. Gen. Stabs. Offz.

The candidate uses **6 observed-coordinate substitutions**, **18 source-mask fills** and **0 unprinted-coordinate fills**. Its remaining zero-based plaintext-position domains are `10: 569PTX`, `11: 248CIM`. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

The earlier **FLUGZEUG** candidate is retained in the [alternative ledger](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/editorial_alternatives.json).
Independent review found that **FAHRZEUG** reduces the observed-coordinate
cost from ten to six while keeping all eighteen source-mask fills and both
reference unknowns. This comparison favors the displayed candidate without
proving that every word is uniquely historical. No missing reporting verb
is added to the stream or the readable display.

## Telefunken inquiry about returning personnel

**Sources on this page:** p112 B. [Concise case study](../radio/telefunken_staff_inquiry.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-telefunken-staff-inquiry-telefunken-inquiry-about-returning-personnel"></a>



**Status:** a complete unchanged-source reading of p112 B. The source has
188 valid coordinates; the old OCR had 189. The native frame yields all
94 positions without a substitution, fill, insertion or deletion.

## Conditional Constantza station-shutdown notice

**Sources on this page:** p112 C. [Concise case study](../radio/constantza_station_shutdown.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-constantza-station-shutdown-conditional-constantza-station-shutdown-notice"></a>


**Status:** a readable conditional edition of p112 C. The enlarged
[source](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/sources/p112_C_detail.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)
clearly advertises 122 coordinates but contains only 110. Its two short
groups are `DVAX` and `AGFF`. A source-preserving 122-slot model adds twelve
unprinted coordinates; their values are not an observed continuation.

The selected frame adds ten coordinates before the visible stream, one
after DVAX and one inside AGFF. No printed marker independently proves
the missing prefix. All **161,025 parameter configurations** in the declared short-group
and two-five-block family are evaluated. They represent **155,400 distinct
source-origin layouts**, with 5,625 duplicate configurations where inserted
positions coalesce. Against the displayed candidate,
this is the only one-cost layout in that family. Allowing twelve arbitrary
missing coordinates gives **eight** equally cheap layouts, all retained.
A minimum for one chosen text does not prove unique wording or loss history.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-constantza-station-shutdown-p112-c"></a>

### p112 C

The header is OUI v OSM, received at 5.59 p.m. on November 4, origin (4) 1700. The readable passage follows the priced edited stream, including its loss assumptions. The literal spelling CONSTANTZA and abbreviation NACHRCHEF are retained in the readable display.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 122-slot loss frame:**

```text
NAC?RCWE?XCO?STA?TZA?EITH?UTE?400AUSS?RB?TRI?B?ESETZTX?ILMISS
```

**Edited output — priced editorial candidate under the same stated frame:**

```text
NACHRCHEFXCONSTANTZASEITHEUTE?400AUSSERBETRIEBGESETZTXMILMISS
```

</details>

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> Nachrchef. Constantza seit heute ?400 außer Betrieb gesetzt. Milmiss.

The candidate uses **1 observed-coordinate substitution**, **0 source-mask fills** and **11 unprinted-coordinate fills**. Its remaining zero-based plaintext-position domains are `29: 0578CX`. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

The unknown position in `?400` has exact domain **0578CX**. Even under a
separate decimal-only assumption, it permits four values; no specific hour
is selected. The quoted time-like field keeps one question mark.

The [complete optional language screen](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/language_screen.json)
ranks every declared parameter configuration without a known plaintext. Its fresh synthetic
controls and failed 112-slot diagnostic frames remain separate from the
fixed-candidate cost proof. A high language rank is a lead, not an independent
source witness.

<a id="edition-cases-military-turkish-armistice-straits-notice-turkish-armistice-and-the-dardanellesbosporus-notice"></a>



**Status:** a native 230-slot source edition of p112 D, with six observed
coordinate substitutions, one printed-dash fill and one unresolved final
position. It describes the straits opening to the Entente after a Turkish
